video_script.title: Missed Connections — Western Water, Spring 2026
video_script.hook: The National Weather Service doesn't usually issue heat stroke and hypothermia warnings for the same location on the same day.
body_slides: March 17th: thermometers break 100 on dry ground.
Same river, same day: snowmelt runs death-cold below.
The weather service had no warning for both.
video_script.voiceover_text: March 17th: Colorado river hits 100 degrees on the bank, snowmelt cold enough to kill you in the water. Same afternoon, same stretch of river. The weather service had no name for it. March 17th: thermometers break 100 on dry ground. Same river, same day: snowmelt runs death-cold below. The weather service had no warning for both. Every part of the water cycle arrived looking for something that had already left. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.
